title: Scorefolio

candidates.name: Scorefolio
candidates.why: A pronounceable score-plus-folio coinage says organised music pages rather than generic scanning; it is short enough for every declared locale and needs a trademark search before release.

candidates.name: Score Pages
candidates.why: Clear and searchable, but generic enough to collide with reader and sheet-music listings.

candidates.name: Folio: Score PDF
candidates.why: It names the output, but Folio is too broad a carrier to claim without a collision screen.

candidates.name: Staffstack
candidates.why: A musical-staff compound has character but does not make the PDF-making job immediately clear.

candidates.name: Music Scanner
candidates.why: It is the crowded category phrase already used by Sheet Music Scanner & Reader and Sheet Music Scanner Pro on the measured shelf.

rejected.name: Music Scanner
rejected.reason: It is a bare category phrase already carried by two measured incumbents, so it offers neither distinction nor title headroom.

rejected.name: Score Pages
rejected.reason: It describes the job but is too generic to form a protectable carrier; Scorefolio retains the job association while avoiding the phrase collision.

rejected.name: Folio: Score PDF
rejected.reason: Folio is a broad occupied word and the candidate adds a generic PDF suffix; the name loses the compact radio test without gaining measured search advantage.

audience: Musicians who need to turn photographed paper sheet music into a usable rehearsal PDF for their own tablet, printer, conductor or ensemble.
rationale: MEASURED — the shelf uses literal scanner and reader phrases, including Sheet Music Scanner & Reader and Sheet Music Scanner Pro; Scorefolio deliberately avoids a one-word variation on those titles while retaining the score-page association.
collisionCheck: UNVERIFIED — no trademark-register or dedicated collision screen for Scorefolio has been run; this is not clearance and the owner must decide after a class-9 search.
localisationCheck: INFERRED — Scorefolio is 10 Latin characters, leaving 20 characters under Play's 30-character title cap for en-US and ru-RU; discoverability of the Latin coinage in Cyrillic search is unmeasured.

scoringRubric.floor: chosen >= 70 with no dimension below 2.5; a hard collision check outranks the score

assumptionsUnverified: Scorefolio has not been searched in trademark registers or a dedicated Play collision screen.
No observed data says that a coined title outperforms the descriptive alternatives for this shelf.
